The City of
OKLAHOMA CITY
TO: Mayor and City Council
FROM: Craig Freeman, City Manager
Resolution authorizing the sole source purchase of four ScanX Scout X-Ray systems from Scanna
MSC, Inc. (SS24-C244005), estimated cost $100,000.
Background:
The Oklahoma City Police Department’s Bomb Squad Unit has a need to purchase four ScanX
Scout X-Ray systems. Currently, the Department has three mounted Logos X-Ray units, which are
no longer being supported by Logos. The Logos system and the Scanna ScanX Scout system are
the only two systems being trained on at the FBI Hazardous Devices School (HDS). The HDS is
ran by the FBI and is the only certification school in the United States for Public Safety Bomb
Technicians. Department staff have attended HDS since 1971. All new Bomb Technicians must
obtain their certifications through the HDS and recertify every three years through HDS.
These mounted systems will be used in four response vehicles. This will allow each response
vehicle to run a full bomb call as per departmental standards. These devices will increase the
OKCPD’s capability in the event of multiple incidents simultaneously.
The use of the mounted systems outweighs the use of the Digital dismounted systems for bomb
calls outside of large events such as the Memorial Marathon. Parts of the city have a lot of radio
frequency interference that sometimes render the dismounted systems useless. This radio
frequency interference does not affect the mounted systems. There is still a great use for the
dismounted systems, however the mounted systems are the staple of necessary equipment for a
bomb squad to complete its mission.
Scanna MSC, Inc. is the sole source provider of the Scanx Scout X-Ray systems. Staff requests
Council authorize the one-time sole source purchase of four Scanx Scout X-Ray systems from
Scanna MSC, Inc. (SS24-C244005), estimated cost $100,000.

OKLAHOMA CITY
TO: Mayor and City Council
FROM: Craig Freeman, City Manager
Concurrence with the Oklahoma City Water Utilities Trust in adopting a Resolution authorizing
the sole source purchase of IDEXX laboratory products for water quality testing from IDEXX
Distribution, Inc. (SS24-C249011), estimated annual cost $125,000, January 1, 2024 through
December 31, 2024.
Purpose:
To authorize the sole source purchase of IDEXX laboratory products.
Background:
The Utilities Department Laboratory (lab) at the Hefner Water Treatment Plant is a municipal
drinking water and wastewater testing laboratory. The lab performs routine water quality testing,
which includes wet chemistry, bacteriological and instrumentation analysis. The lab is certified by
the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality to conduct tests using IDEXX products. This
testing protocol is necessary to meet the requirements for safe drinking water.
IDEXX is considered a sole source vendor because there are no other equivalent products on the
market, and IDEXX does not sell its products for environmental testing in the United States
through third-party vendors. Without these products, the lab would have to go through a re-
certification process to change the testing protocol.
Staff recommends the sole source resolution be adopted so that water and wastewater quality
testing can continue in accordance with state regulations.

FROM: Craig Freeman, City Manager
Resolution authorizing the sole source purchase of MAGNUSWorx Peak Performance and
Wellness Application from Readiness Network, Inc. dba International Academy of Public Safety
(SS25-C254006), estimated cost $140,000, January 31, 2024 through January 30, 2025.
Purpose:
To provide the Oklahoma City Police Department Wellness Unit with an application that will
amplify their efforts in providing unlimited health and wellness resources for employees.
Background:
The Police Department has a continuous need for wellness related services for police officers and
their families. These customized wellness services include facing the unique challenges when
dealing with mental health, emotional resiliency, physical fitness, sleep, hygiene, and couples
communication.
Currently, the Department’s Wellness Unit includes four full-time staff members, one Licensed
Professional Counselor (LPC) and about 45 part-time peers currently serving roughly 1,200 sworn
officers, plus 300-400 civilian employees and their families. The Wellness Unit has set a goal of
serving 2,800 to 3,200 Police Department employees and their families.
MAGNUSWorx Peak Performance and Wellness application content can be customized to help
employees maximize the benefits from using this application. The content is specifically geared
toward assisting the user with whatever issues or needs they may have as well as maintaining the
confidentiality of the user. This application also allows for content to be customized specifically
for the Police Department and the unique mental health challenges faced by officers.
Staff requests Council approve the sole source purchase of MAGNUSWorx Peak Performance and
Wellness Application from Readiness Network, Inc. dba International Academy of Public Safety
(SS25-C254006), estimated cost $140,000, January 31, 2024 through January 30, 2025.

through other providers. This program has unique features built into the application that is unlike
any other program available.
Police employees will be able to access the content within the application 24/7 for all their
Wellness needs. All employees are empowered to take control of their own emotional and mental
health growth by having access to the 11 Rings of Wellness library. The 11 Rings are
Relationship Development, Family Dynamics, Spiritual Being, Mental Toughness, Emotional
Balance, Physical Strength, Resilience Fitness, Financial Stability, Occupational Fulfillment,
Leadership Capacities, and Social Connections. Each category is supported by subject matter
experts teaching others how to build antifragility and resiliency into their personal lives.
The application will also be able to collect data from users to provide content specifically geared
to assist the user with whatever issues or needs they may have. To date, the department has not
located a Wellness Application which used searched data input to deliver personalized content.
Two additional categories this application covers are Bulletproof Spirit Wellness and West
Point Leadership.

COTPA-RFP 26-004 Bus Rapid Transit Bus Purchase
Recipient- Central Oklahoma Transportation and Parking Authority (“COTPA”)
Determination:
This written determination documents the results of the Pre-Award Audit required under 49 CFR
§§ 663.21–663.27 for the procurement of revenue-service rolling stock using Federal Transit
Administration (FTA) funds. Only one proposal was received in response to the solicitation issued
on April 15, 2026. After review and evaluation, the Recipient has determined that awarding to
New Flyer is appropriate and compliant with federal requirements.
Findings:
1. Pre-Award Audit Completion
The Recipient has completed the required pre-award audit prior to entering into a formal contract
for rolling stock. This audit includes:
 A pre-award Buy America certification confirming compliance or the existence of an
applicable FTA waiver, as required under 49 CFR § 663.25.
 A pre-award purchaser’s requirements certification confirming that the proposed rolling
stock meets the technical specifications outlined in the solicitation and that the
manufacturer is responsible and capable, as required under 49 CFR § 663.27.
2. Single Proposal Receipt and Evaluation
Although only one proposal was received, the Recipient reviewed the proposal according to the
solicitation’s evaluation criteria and determined that:
 The procurement process was followed to receive competitive proposals.
 The single proposer, New Flyer, is responsive and responsible.
 The offered vehicle conforms to all required technical specifications of the RFP.
 Price is fair and reasonable based on ICE, available market data and procurement history
in compliance with 2 CFR 200.324(a–b) and FTA Circular 4220.1G.
Independent Cost Estimate (ICE)
Recipient has completed the required ICE: The ICE form has been reviewed and approved by the
DBE Coordinator, IT Manager, Finance, Grants administrator and Administrator to ensure that it
meets the Scope of Work/Technical Specifications and all other documentation as required in the
RFP.
Competitive Price Analysis
Price analysis was obtained from the latestcost.com as it compares the City Bus Purchase Costs
and Price Ranges 2026 and it presents clear cost ranges and factors that influence the final price to
help buyers estimate a budget. This information was used to complete the ICE form as pricing is
$896,570 per 40-foot CNG bus which is below the average price of $1,000,000 for a single 40-
foot bus.
3. Compliance with Federal Requirements
Even with a single proposal, federal regulations require documentation demonstrating compliance
with pre-award audit obligations. The Recipient has verified all required information from the
manufacturer concerning Buy America components, final assembly location, and compliance with
applicable safety certifications as outlined in 49 CFR Part 663 Subpart B.
Conclusion:
COTPA determines that New Flyer’s proposal is reasonable and justified considering the
procurement process and price. New Flyer’s proposal is acceptably priced at $15,000,000.00. It is
in the best interest of Recipient to proceed with award, contingent upon final Board review and
approval.

MEMORANDUM
OCAT Agenda
Item No. IV. S
6/25/2026
TO: Trustees, Oklahoma City Airport Trust
FROM: Jeff Mulder, Director of Airports
Resolution waiving formal competitive bidding and ratifying the actions of the Director of Airports
in approving a sole source purchase with Office Interiors, LLC for material and labor of Projects
OCAT WRWA 2507, Common Use Gates & Ticket Counters, $440,100.15; Landside Furniture
Baggage, $177,495.51; and Landside Furniture Ticketing, $17,079.31; estimated total cost
$634,674.97.
Location:
OKC Will Rogers International Airport
Background:
The hold room seating for Common Use Gates 20, 22 and 24 is in poor condition. Power to chairs
does not work, and the chairs need to be updated with the same type of seating currently utilized
in the rest of the Terminal in order for chairs to be interchangeable as needed. In addition, the hold
room-type seating in the Landside Baggage and Ticketing areas is also in poor condition.
Office Interiors, LLC is currently the sole authorized distributor in the State of Oklahoma
authorized by Kusch+Co GmbH to purchase, resell, install, and maintain their products. As such,
staff recommend the Trust waive formal competitive bidding and approve a sole source purchase
order with Office Interiors, LLC for the material and labor, estimated cost $634,674.97.
Kush-Co GmbH products are the current hold room seating products across the airport. It is in the
Trust’s best interest to purchase the same products to provide consistency in the Terminal.
Recommendation: Resolution be adopted.

RESOLUTION WAIVING FORMAL COMPETITIVE BIDDING AND
RATIFYING THE ACTIONS OF THE DIRECTOR OF AIRPORTS IN
APPROVING A SOLE SOURCE PURCHASE WITH OFFICE INTERIORS,
LLC FOR MATERIAL AND LABOR OF PROJECTS OCAT WRWA
2507, COMMON USE GATES & TICKET COUNTERS,
$440,100.15; LANDSIDE FURNITURE BAGGAGE, $177,495.51; AND

WHEREAS, the Oklahoma City Airport Trust (“Trust”) is a public trust, created pursuant to its
Trust Indenture under the authority of laws of the State of Oklahoma; and with the City of
Oklahoma City (“City”) is its sole beneficiary; and
WHEREAS, the Trust leases, manages, and operates certain real estate for the City commonly
known as OKC Will Rogers International Airport (“Airport”), which is located in Oklahoma and
Cleveland Counties, Oklahoma; and
WHEREAS, the Trust has a need to update hold room, baggage and ticketing seating to match the
rest of the terminal seating, and provide seating with power; and
WHEREAS, Office Interiors LLC is currently the sole authorized distributor in the State of
Oklahoma authorized by Kusch+Co GmbH to purchase, resell, install, and maintain all Kusch+Co
GmbH products; and
WHEREAS, Kusch+Co GmbH products are the current hold room seating products across the
Airport and purchasing the same products will provide consistency and ability to interchange the
hold room, baggage and ticketing seating across the Airport as the need arises; and
WHEREAS, staff recommend the Trust waive formal competitive bidding and approve a sole
source purchase with Office Interiors LLC for the materials and labor of the hold room, baggage
and ticketing seating, estimated cost of $634,674.97.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Oklahoma City Airport Trust that the Trust
hereby waives formal competitive bidding and ratifies the actions of the Director of Airports in
approving the sole source purchase with Office Interiors, LLC for the material and labor of Projects
OCAT WRWA 2507, Common Use Gates & Ticket Counters, $440,100.15; Landside Furniture

TO: Chairperson and Board of Trustees
FROM: Administrator
Approve Renewal No. 3 of Sole Source Professional Services Agreement with B&C Transit
Company, Inc., for software, hardware, and ongoing system support for Supervisory Control and
Data Acquisition System (SCADA) services for OKC Streetcar, estimated annual cost of
$100,000, June 1, 2026 through May 31, 2027.
Background:
The Central Oklahoma Transportation and Parking Authority (COTPA) has a continuing need to
update software and hardware for the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system
to maintain and operate the OKC Streetcar system safely.
COTPA implemented the SCADA system using B&C Transit Company, Inc. (B&C) in 2018 with
the launch of the OKC Streetcar. The SCADA system helps ensure the safe operation of an
overhead catenary system that powers the OKC Streetcar system. B&C is the only firm authorized
to offer software, hardware, maintenance, and technical support services for OKC Streetcar’s
SCADA system.
On June 2, 2023 (Item No. VI. B.), COTPA entered into a sole source professional services
agreement with B&C for one year ending on May 31, 2024, with four additional one-year renewal
options.
On May 3, 2024 (Item No. V. B.), the COTPA Board approved Renewal No. 1 for the period
ending May 31, 2025.
On May 9, 2025 (Item No. V. B.), the COTPA Board approved Renewal No. 2 for the period
ending May 31, 2026.
Staff recommends approval of Renewal No. 3 with B&C Transit Inc., for the period of June 1,
2026, through May 31, 2027, estimated cost of $100,000.

SUBJECT: Sole Source Purchase Justification for Supervisory Control and
Data Acquisition (SCADA) system
In the development and construction of the OKC Streetcar, the construction
general contractor purchased and integrated the SCADA system from B&C
Transit Company, Inc (B&C) for software and hardware to manage the safe
operation of the Overhead Catenary System (OCS) that powers the OKC
Streetcar system. The development and implementation of the SCADA system
was a part of the overall contract with our OKC Streetcar general contractor of
construction Herzog/Stacy Witbeck and Joint Venture.
B&C Transit Company System, Inc.’s SCADA system should be considered
sole source as OKC Streetcar has been using the SCADA system since
operation began in 2018. Changing the system at this point would cause
undue hardship and be a cost burden to redevelop, implement and launch a
new SCADA system.
Central Oklahoma Transportation and Parking Authority (COTPA) entered into
a Sole Source Professional Service Agreement with B&C (COTPA SS25-
C244100). The Agreement was for one year with four additional one-year
renewal options. On May 3, 2024 (Item No. V.B.), the COTPA Board approved
Renewal No. 1, extending the Professional Service Agreement for one year
ending May 31, 2025. On May 9, 2025 (Item No. V.B.), the COTPA Board
approved Renewal No. 2, extending the Professional Service Agreement for
one year ending May 31, 2025. This is the third of four (4) one-year renewal
option.
The sole source renewal with B&C Transit Company, Inc. will be
approximately $100,000 for continued software, hardware, maintenance,
and technical support services for the OKC Streetcar’s SCADA system.

Resolution authorizing the sole source purchase of CNG compressor parts from Angi Energy
Systems, LLC (COKC02190), estimated cost $100,000, October 7, 2025 through October 6, 2026.
Purpose:
To provide the Oklahoma City General Services Department/Fleet Division with proprietary parts
to repair/rebuild two CNG compressors for the Central Maintenance Facility (CMF). Without the
repairs to the CMF compressors, staff will be unable to refuel the City’s fleet of CNG vehicles.
Background:
The General Services Department/Fleet Services Division operates and maintains two compressors
which serve both the slow and fast-fill CNG fuel dispensers at the Central Maintenance Facility.
Both compressors are original to the CNG fuel site, which was installed in 2011 (MC-0431). The
proprietary parts needed to refurbish both compressors cost approximately $97,500.
Angi Energy Systems, LLC is the only supplier that can provide the computer programming and
necessary parts to operate and refurbish the equipment. Therefore, staff requests Council authorize
the sole source purchase of CNG compressor parts from Angi Energy Systems, LLC
(COKC02190), estimated cost $100,000, October 7, 2025 through October 6, 2026.

TO: Chairperson and Board of Trustees
FROM: Administrator
Approve Renewal No. 2 with B&C Transit Company, Inc. (COTPA - SS25-C244100), for
software, hardware, and ongoing system support for the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition
System (SCADA) services for OKC Streetcar, estimated annual cost of $100,000, June 1, 2025
through May 31, 2026.
Background:
The Central Oklahoma Transportation and Parking Authority (COTPA) has a continuing need to
update software and hardware for the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system
to maintain and operate the OKC Streetcar system safely.
COTPA implemented the SCADA system using B&C Transit Company, Inc. (B&C). The SCADA
system helps ensure the safe operation of an overhead catenary system that powers the streetcars.
B&C is the only firm authorized to offer software, hardware, maintenance, and technical support
services for the OKC Streetcar’s SCADA system. On June 2, 2023 (Item No. VI.B.), COTPA
entered into a sole source professional service agreement with B&C (COTPA SS25-C244100).
The agreement was for one year with four additional one-year renewal options. On May 3, 2024
(Item No. V.B.), the COTPA Board approved Renewal No. 1, extending the professional service
agreement for one year ending May 31, 2025. This is the second renewal option.

SUBJECT: Sole Source Purchase Justification for Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition
(SCADA) system
In the development and construction of the OKC Streetcar, the construction general contractor
purchased and integrated the SCADA system from B&C Transit Company, Inc (B&C) for
software and hardware to manage the safe operation of the Overhead Catenary System (OCS) that
powers the OKC Streetcar system. The development and implementation of the SCADA system
was a part of the overall contract with our OKC Streetcar general contractor of construction
Herzog/Stacy Witbeck and Joint Venture.
B&C Transit Company System, Inc.’s SCADA system should be considered sole source as OKC
Streetcar has been using the SCADA system since operation began in 2018. Changing the system
at this point would cause undue hardship and be a cost burden to redevelop, implement and
launch a new SCADA system.
COTPA entered into a Sole Source Professional Service Agreement with B&C (COTPA SS25-
C244100). The Agreement was for one year with four additional one-year renewal options. On
May 3, 2024 (Item No. V.B.), the COTPA Board approved Renewal No. 1, extending the
Professional Service Agreement for one year ending May 31, 2025. This is the second renewal
option.
The sole source renewal with B&C Transit Company, Inc. will be approximately $100,000 for
continued software, hardware, maintenance, and technical support services for the OKC
Streetcar’s SCADA system.
Jesse Rush / COTPA Administrator
Central Oklahoma Transportation & Parking Authority

to upgrade and migrate the on-premise Selectron Relay Permits IVR, SelecTXT, and Atlas Insight

Background:
On August 13, 2013 (Item No. MFA.A.), the Oklahoma City Municipal Facilities Authority
(OCMFA) adopted a resolution for the purchase and implementation of an interactive voice
response (IVR) system to integrate with Accela; and approved a Software License Agreement, and
Support and Maintenance Agreement with Selectron Technologies, Inc., August 13, 2013 through
August 31, 2020.
Accela is the integrated planning, permits and licensing information system utilized by The City
of Oklahoma City (City). The integrated IVR system provides an alternative and more efficient
process than manually requesting inspections for permits via phone or fax. In addition, Selectron
Technologies has SelecTXT, the only application for inspection scheduling via test messaging,
and Atlas Insight, the only application for workforce efficiency monitoring, capable of interface
with Accela.
On October 19, 2018 (Item No. MFA.A.), the OCMFA approved the Sole Source Agreement with
Selectron Technologies, Inc. and adopted a resolution to ratify the purchase of SelecTXT and Atlas
Insight, October 9, 2018 through March 31, 2019.
On May 26, 2020, (Item No. MFA.E.), the OCMFA entered into a Professional Services
Agreement with Selectron Technologies, Inc., to provide interactive voice response system
support, maintenance, and related products and services, May 26, 2020 through March 31, 2025.
Staff recommends approval of Amendment No. 1 to allow the upgrade and migration of the on-
premise Selectron Relay Permits IVR, SelecTXT, and Atlas Insight software into Selectron's
hosted environment, and extending the term of the Professional Services Agreement for an
additional 5 -year term, April 1, 2025 through March 31, 2030.

units, and repair services for various machinery.

Specifications were advertised in the Journal Record and posted in the electronic bidding system.
Thirty-three potential bidders viewed the bid, with five bids submitted. The bids were evaluated

services for various machinery not available on pricing agreements, estimated annual cost
$500,000, August 1, 2024 through July 31, 2027.

procedures, which the Oklahoma City Water Utilities Trust has adopted.

TO: Trustees, Oklahoma City Water Utilities Trust
FROM: Chris Browning, General Manager
1. Pricing Agreements award and approval, All State Electric Motors, LLC (OCWUT00046),
Cogent, Inc. (OCWUT00047), Edwards Equipment, LLC (OCWUT00048), Environmental
Improvements, Inc. (OCWUT00049), and Haynes Equipment Company, LLC
(OCWUT00050), replacement parts, units, and repair services for various machinery,
estimated annual cost $4,000,000, August 1, 2024 through July 31, 2027; and
2. Resolution authorizing the open market purchase of replacement parts, units, and repair
services for various machinery not available on pricing agreements, estimated annual cost
$500,000, August 1, 2024 through July 31, 2027.
Purpose:
To award pricing agreements and to authorize the open market purchase of replacement parts,
units, and repair services for various machinery.
Background:
Specifications were advertised in the Journal Record and posted in the electronic bidding system.
Thirty-three potential bidders viewed the bid, with five bids submitted. The bids were evaluated
based on the award methodology set forth in the specifications.
Staff recommends multiple awards to five bidders to ensure adequate coverage of the commodities.
Staff also requests open market authority for the purchase of replacement parts, units, and repair
services for various machinery not available on pricing agreements, estimated annual cost
$500,000, August 1, 2024 through July 31, 2027.
Purchases made with this authority will comply with the City’s open market purchasing
procedures, which the Oklahoma City Water Utilities Trust has adopted.

PURCHASE OF REPLACEMENT PARTS, UNITS, AND
REPAIR SERVICES FOR VARIOUS MACHINERY NOT
AVAILABLE ON PRICING AGREEMENTS, ESTIMATED
ANNUAL COST $500,000, AUGUST 1, 2024 THROUGH
JULY 31, 2027.
WHEREAS, specifications were advertised in the Journal Record and posted in the
electronic bidding system; and
WHEREAS, thirty-three potential bidders viewed the bid, with five bids submitted; and
WHEREAS, the bids were evaluated based on the award methodology set forth in the
specifications; and
WHEREAS, staff recommends multiple awards to five bidders to ensure adequate
coverage of the commodities; and
WHEREAS, staff also requests open market authority for the purchase of replacement
parts, units, and repair services for various machinery not available on pricing agreements,
estimated annual cost $500,000, August 1, 2024, through July 31, 2027; and
WHEREAS, purchases made with this authority will comply with the City’s open
market purchasing procedures, which the Oklahoma City Water Utilities Trust has adopted.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Trustees of the Oklahoma City
Water Utilities Trust that they do hereby authorize the open market purchase of replacement
parts, units, and repair services for various machinery not available on pricing agreements,
estimated annual cost $500,000, August 1, 2024 through July 31, 2027.

OKLAHOMA CITY
TO: Mayor and City Council
FROM: Craig Freeman, City Manager
Resolution approving Cooperative Service Agreement with the United States Department of
Agriculture Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service Wildlife Services (COKC00766), sole
source purchase of a wildlife damage management project work plan, not to exceed $80,000,
October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027.
Purpose:
To provide the Parks and Recreation Department with a wildlife damage management program to
mitigate damage caused by resident waterfowl and aquatic rodents to property and protected
resources by the United States Department of Agriculture.
Background:
A sole source agreement was originally approved November 11, 2023 (Item No. IX.E.) for the
period ended September 30, 2024. The agreement was renewed on September 24, 2024 (Item No.
IX.BH.) for the period ended September 30, 2025. The agreement was approved on September
23, 2025 (Item No. IX. J.) for the period ending September 30, 2026. This Agreement may be
amended and extended by mutual agreement of the parties in writing, prior to expiration of the
agreement. The USDA is a self-insured Federal government entity.
The Parks and Recreation Department has a continuous need for a wildlife damage management
program for Will Rogers Gardens, the Bricktown Canal, Martin Nature Park, and other Parks and
Recreation facilities. This program will mitigate damage caused by resident waterfowl and aquatic
rodents to property and protected resources. Mitigation activities will include employing a variety
of effective tools and techniques in an integrated wildlife damage management operational
program as well as information transfer.
The USDA APHIS-WS is the sole source provider of biological, humane, and economical
practices as they are authorized to use control methods and solutions exclusive to USDA APHIS-
WS. Staff requests sole source authority to use USDA APHIS-WS as their methods also allow for
control efforts to be conducted on large scale locations that require certified specialists due to the
scope of duties.
Staff requests Council approve Cooperative Service Agreement with the United States Department
of Agriculture, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service-Wildlife Services (COKC00766), sole
source purchase of a wildlife damage management project work plan, not to exceed $80,000,

WHEREAS, the purpose of this agreement is to provide the Parks and Recreation
Department with a wildlife damage management program to mitigate damage caused by resident
waterfowl and aquatic rodents to property and protected resources by the United States Department
of Agriculture; and
WHEREAS, Council initially approved this agreement on November 11, 2023 (Item No.
IX. E.) for the period ended September 30, 2024; and
WHEREAS, the agreement was renewed on September 23, 2025 (Item No. IX. J.) for the
period ending September 30, 2026; and
WHEREAS, the USDA is a self-insured Federal Government entity; and
WHEREAS, the Parks and Recreation Department has a continuous need for a wildlife
damage management program for Will Rogers Gardens, the Bricktown Canal, Martin Nature Park,
and other Parks and Recreation facilities; and
WHEREAS, this program will mitigate damage caused by resident waterfowl and aquatic
rodents to property and protected resources; and
WHEREAS, mitigation activities will include employing a variety of effective tools and
techniques in an integrated wildlife damage management operational program as well as
information transfer; and
WHEREAS, the USDA APHIS-WS is the sole source provider of biological, humane, and
economical practices as they are authorized to use control methods and solutions exclusive to
USDA APHIS-WS; and
WHEREAS, staff requests sole source authority to use the USDA APHIS-WS as their
methods also allow for control efforts to be conducted on large scale locations that require certified
specialists due to the scope of duties; and
WHEREAS, staff requests Council approve Cooperative Service Agreement with the
United States Department of Agriculture Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service Wildlife
Services (COKC00766), sole source purchase of a wildlife damage management project work plan,
not to exceed $80,000, October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027; and
WHEREAS, there is a continuing need for the procurement of these services for the Parks
and Recreation Department at multiple facilities.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of The City of Oklahoma City
that they do hereby approve Cooperative Service Agreement with the United States Department of
Agriculture Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service Wildlife Services (COKC00766), sole
source purchase of a wildlife damage management project work plan, not to exceed $80,000,
October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027.
